title: index
content:
The ProteomIQon
ProteomIQon is a set of command line tools for the analysis of mass spectrometry based proteomics data, written in F#.
Each tool does one step and writes plain files that the next tool reads, so a pipeline is a sequence of tool calls
that can be rerun from any point. Most tools append to an output file that already exists, so delete the old
file before rerunning a step into the same directory. The chain covers signal detection, peptide identification,
quantification, retention time alignment between runs and protein inference.

The proteomics theory behind the steps is documented in BioFSharp.Mz, the
library most tools build on. The tool pages here link to it where a concept needs more than a sentence.
Installing a tool
Every tool is a .NET tool on nuget.org, package ProteomIQon.<ToolName>,
command proteomiqon-<toolname>.
dotnet tool install --global ProteomIQon.PeptideDB
proteomiqon-peptidedb --help

Tools that take parameters read them from a JSON file. Each tool page shows the parameters with a script that writes
the file, and the command line calls.
How the tools chain
A run of a data dependent acquisition experiment goes through these steps. Each tool writes the files in its last
column, and the next tool reads them.

Five more tools cover other inputs. For 15N labeled samples, RatioLFQ turns the
light to heavy ratios in LabeledQuant.txt into one intensity per run and protein. For timsTOF data with ion mobility,
MzMLToMzLiteIonMobility converts the mzML, and
MsFraggerToPSM imports an MSFragger search. PeptideSpectrumMatchingTIMs identifies the spectra of an ion
mobility run without MSFragger and writes the .psm that PSMStatistics reads.
PSMBasedQuantificationTIMs quantifies in retention time and ion
mobility from the .qpsm of PSMStatistics or MsFraggerToPSM.
The core project
The ProteomIQon core is referenced by all tools. It contains mainly serializable data transfer objects such as tool results and tool parameters, as well as their mapping to domain specific types.
This is also the place for any kind of code reusable across tools such as thin wrappers around data readers, logging or CLI formatting.
Documentation
The documentation is generated with fsdocs from the .fsx files in the docs folder.
If you find a typo, please submit a pull request. How to document your work explains the setup.
Contributing
Please refer to the CSB Contribution guidelines
Community/Social
Want to get in touch with us? We recently joined the twitter crowd:

Citation
When using ProteomIQon in scientific or commercial releases, please cite us using the DOI 10.5281/zenodo.6335068.

title: How to build binaries or packages
content:
How to build binaries or packages
The build is a FAKE project under build/. build.cmd and build.sh
run it with the target name as the first argument. Without a target it builds the whole
solution.
Building
The Build target compiles every released tool listed in build/ProjectInfo.fs:
.\build.cmd build

The Preprocessing project references packages from the CSBiology feed on GitHub Packages.
nuget.config reads the credentials for that feed from the environment variables GithubUser
and PackageToken. Set both before building the full solution, which includes that project. The
released tools restore from nuget.org alone.
To build a single tool, call dotnet on its project file:
dotnet build src/PeptideDB/PeptideDB.fsproj -c Release

Packing
The Pack target creates a NuGet package for every released project in pkg/. The version
comes from the top entry of each project's RELEASE_NOTES.md that has a version, so bump that file
first. A leading #### Unreleased section without a version collects changes until the next release
and is skipped; replace it with the version and the date when you release:
.\build.cmd pack

PackPrerelease does the same with a suffix it asks for on the console. Every tool packs as a
.NET tool with the package id ProteomIQon.<ToolName> and the command name
proteomiqon-<toolname>. A package from pkg/ can be installed locally to try it out before
publishing:
dotnet tool install --global ProteomIQon.PeptideDB --add-source ./pkg --version 0.0.10

Published versions are on nuget.org.
Tests
RunTests builds and runs tests/ProteomIQon.Tests.fsproj. The end to end pipeline tests
start the tool assemblies, so this target needs the full build to succeed first:
.\build.cmd runtests
headings: How to build binaries or packages

title: How to document your work
content:
How to document your work
The pages on this site are literate F# scripts under docs/, rendered with the
fsdocs tool. Prose lives in (** ... *)
comment blocks as markdown, code between the blocks is shown with syntax highlighting and
tooltips.
Building the docs locally
From the repository root, restore the tools once and then run the docs target. It builds the
core project in Release and renders the site into output/:
dotnet tool restore
.\build.cmd builddocs

On Linux or macOS use ./build.sh builddocs. For editing with hot reload use the watch target.
It serves the site on a local port and re-renders a page whenever you save it:
.\build.cmd watchdocs

The rendered pages link their stylesheet with the absolute site root. Open them through the
watch server. Opened from disk they load without a stylesheet.
Adding a page for a tool
Copy an existing file from docs/tools/, for example PeptideDB.fsx, rename it after the tool
folder in src/, and adjust the frontmatter at the top. index sets the position in the
sidebar. The pages are ordered along the processing chain, so pick the slot where the new tool
fits and shift the later ones if needed.
Each tool page has the same four parts: a short description of what the tool does and where it
sits in the chain, an inputs and outputs section, the parameter table with the defaults from
src/ProteomIQon/defaultParams/, and the script that writes a parameter file followed by the
command line calls. Tools without a parameter file skip the table and the script. Keep the parameter script runnable. It references the core assembly built
by builddocs, so this proves it before you publish:
dotnet fsi docs/tools/YourTool.fsx

BioFSharp.Mz already explains the theory, and the pages link to it. The
BioFSharp.Mz documentation covers signal detection,
search databases, scoring, FDR control, quantification and protein inference.
Publishing
Pushing changes under docs/, build/ or src/ProteomIQon/ to the dev branch triggers the Deploy Docs GitHub Action.
It runs the same builddocs target and pushes output/ to the gh-pages branch, which
GitHub Pages serves at csbiology.github.io/ProteomIQon.
The workflow can also be started by hand from the Actions tab.
headings: Adding a page for a tool

title: How to create your own tool
content:
How to create a tool
Every ProteomIQon tool is a small console project under src/ with the same three files:
CLIArgumentParsing.fs declares the command line arguments with
Argu, Program.fs parses them, reads the parameter JSON
and loops over the input files, and a third file holds the actual work. Parameter records and
result row types shared between tools live in the core project src/ProteomIQon/.
Scaffolding from the template
The repository ships a dotnet new template that creates this layout. Install it once from
the repository root:
dotnet new install ./ConsoleTemplate/template

dotnet new list should now show pct (prototypical proteomiqon console project). Create the
project inside src/ and add it to the solution:
cd src
dotnet new pct -n MyTool --force
cd ..
dotnet sln ProteomIQon.sln add src/MyTool/MyTool.fsproj

Compare the new .fsproj with a current tool such as src/PeptideDB/PeptideDB.fsproj and take
the target framework, the package versions, the PackAsTool and ToolCommandName properties
from there.
Wiring the tool in
Four more places need to know about the tool:


A parameter record in src/ProteomIQon/DTO.fs with a toDomain conversion, plus a default
JSON file in src/ProteomIQon/defaultParams/. The tools read parameters with
Json.ReadAndDeserialize.

A RELEASE_NOTES.md in the project folder. The build reads the package version from it.
An entry in the projects list of build/ProjectInfo.fs, so Build and Pack include it.
A page in docs/tools/, see How to document your work.

Then open a pull request against dev.

title: MsFraggerToPSM
content:
MsFraggerToPSM
MsFraggerToPSM turns the psm.tsv result of an MSFragger search, as written by FragPipe, into the .qpsm files that PSMBasedQuantificationTIMs reads.
With it, an ion mobility run can be identified in FragPipe and quantified in ProteomIQon, in place of the PeptideSpectrumMatching and PSMStatistics pair.
For each row of the tsv the tool rebuilds the modified peptide sequence in ProteomIQon notation, looks it up in the PeptideDB database to get the peptide and modified sequence identifiers, and assigns the row to an MS2 spectrum of the mzlite. Among the spectra of the same charge (or without charge) it takes the one whose scan time and precursor m/z lie closest to the values in the tsv, and it looks first among those whose ion mobility is within 0.001 of the tsv value. A row without any spectrum of its charge is dropped.
The tool has no parameter file.
Inputs and outputs



Flag
Meaning
Comes from




-i
one or more psm.tsv files, or a directory that is searched for *.tsv
MSFragger (FragPipe)


-ii
the matching .mzlite files, or a directory that is searched for *.mzlite
MzMLToMzLiteIonMobility


-o
the output directory, created when missing



-d
the SQLite peptide database
PeptideDB


-c
number of pairs converted at the same time, default 1





All four flags are mandatory. The tsv needs the columns Assigned Modifications, Peptide, Retention, Charge, Calibrated Observed M/Z, Calculated Peptide Mass, Delta Mass, Peptide Length, Number of Missed Cleavages, Hyperscore, Probability and Protein, and should have Ion Mobility. Retention is read in seconds and stored in minutes.
Files are paired by position, the first tsv with the first mzlite and so on. Give both lists in the same order and with the same length, otherwise the tool converts nothing.
The tool stops when the database file does not exist. The lookup uses the unlabeled sequences of the database. Rows whose modified sequence has no entry in the database are dropped, so the database has to be built with the same modifications as the FragPipe search.
From the Assigned Modifications column the tool understands oxidized methionine and carbamidomethylated cysteine, plus N-terminal acetylation. A row with any other modification is printed to the console and dropped.
The tool writes one <run>.qpsm per mzlite into the output directory, named after the mzlite. It has the column layout of the .qpsm of PSMStatistics, with one row per identified spectrum and the spectrum identifier of the mzlite as PSMId. ScanNr is the position of that spectrum among the MS2 spectra in scan time order, Label is 1 and GlobalMod is 0. ModelScore is the FragPipe probability, PEPValue is 1 minus the probability and QValue is the mean PEPValue of all rows of the tsv with an equal or lower PEPValue. XtandemScore is the MSFragger hyperscore, and the other search scores are NaN. PSMBasedQuantificationTIMs takes the ion mobility from the spectrum.
An existing .qpsm of the same name is appended to. Delete the old file before a rerun.
The output directory also receives MSFraggerToPSM_log.txt.
Running the tool
Install the tool with dotnet tool install --global ProteomIQon.MsFraggerToPSM, then convert one run:
proteomiqon-msfraggertopsm -i path/to/run/psm.tsv -ii path/to/run.mzlite -d path/to/AraTest.db -o path/to/output

Several runs, paired by position and converted three at a time:
proteomiqon-msfraggertopsm -i path/to/run1/psm.tsv path/to/run2/psm.tsv path/to/run3/psm.tsv -ii path/to/run1.mzlite path/to/run2.mzlite path/to/run3.mzlite -d path/to/AraTest.db -o path/to/output -c 3

All flags:
proteomiqon-msfraggertopsm --help

title: PSMBasedQuantification
content:
PSMBasedQuantification
PSMBasedQuantification turns the identifications from PSMStatistics into peptide ion intensities.
For every identified peptide ion (sequence, modification state and charge) it takes the scan times of its MS/MS identifications, extracts an ion chromatogram of the monoisotopic m/z in a window around them, detects the peaks in that trace and fits the peak that contains the weighted scan time of its identifications (see CentrePSMs and RequirePeakAtScanTime). The fitted area is the reported quantity.
For metabolically labeled samples the tool computes the m/z of the partner ion (the heavy form of a light identification, or the other way round) and quantifies that trace as well, so every row can carry a light and a heavy value.

Inputs and outputs



Flag
Meaning
Comes from




-i
one or more .mzlite files, or a directory
MzMLToMzLite


-ii
one or more .qpsm files, or a directory that is searched for *.qpsm
PSMStatistics


-d
the SQLite peptide database
PeptideDB


-o
the output directory, created when missing



-p
the parameter file in JSON
this page


-mf
switch: pair files by base name instead of by position



-dc
switch: write diagnostic charts



-z
switch: pack the chart directory into a zip file and delete it



-c
number of runs quantified at the same time, default 1





The input must be .mzlite. A directory given to -i is also scanned for .mzML, but the tool opens every file with the mzlite reader and fails on anything else, so convert first.
With one file per flag the pair is used as given. With lists, the n-th mzlite file is paired with the n-th qpsm file unless you pass -mf, which pairs files by their base name (run1.mzlite with run1.qpsm) and skips mzlite files without a partner.
For every run the tool writes run.quant, tab separated with a header and one row per quantified peptide ion. Next to the identifiers and the best q-value and PEP value of the ion it reports the fitted quantity (Quant_Light, Quant_Heavy), the apex intensity, the fit parameters, the difference between identification and fitted scan time, the extracted traces and the isotope pattern for both channels.
QuantBasedAlignment, AlignmentBasedQuantification, AlignmentBasedQuantStatistics and JoinQuantPepIonsWithProteins read .quant files.
With -dc the tool writes one chart per peptide ion into run_plots, plus mzErrorAndCorrection.html for the m/z calibration it derives from the identifications. -z packs that directory into run_plots.zip and deletes it. Delete an existing run.quant in the output directory before a rerun, the tool appends to it. Logs go to PSMBasedQuantification_log.txt and run_log.txt in the output directory.
Parameters



Parameter
Default
Meaning




PerformLabeledQuantification
Labeling.N15Labeling
Unlabeled quantifies only the identified ion. N15Labeling quantifies the partner ion too and keeps rows where both fits pass the quality filter. N15LabelingOnly applies the filter to the heavy channel alone. Labelshift quantifies both and skips the filter.


XicExtraction.ScanTimeWindow
2.0
Half width of the scan time window around the identification that is extracted and searched for the peak, in the scan time unit of the run.


XicExtraction.MzWindow_Da
Window.Estimate
Half width of the m/z window of the trace, in Da, the same at every m/z. The trace is centred on the m/z corrected by an offset that the tool fits on the precursor m/z of the identifications, in ppm over retention time and m/z. Estimate uses four times the standard deviation of the difference between the measured and theoretical precursor m/z of the identifications, leaving out outliers. Window.Fixed 0.07 sets 0.07 Da.


XicExtraction.XicProcessing
XicProcessing.Wavelet waveletParams
Peak detection on the trace. The wavelet parameters are listed below. SecondDerivative is the other supported case. Gabor3D is in development and does not work currently.


XicExtraction.TopKPSMs
None
Some k keeps only the k identifications with the highest ModelScore per peptide ion when placing the scan time.


XicExtraction.IonMobilityWindow
Window.Fixed 0.05
Not used, the tool does not read ion mobility.


BaseLineCorrection
Some { MaxIterations = 10; Lambda = 6; P = 0.05 }
Asymmetric least squares baseline subtraction on the trace before peak detection. None skips it.


QualityFilterLog2Limit
2.0
The quality filter keeps rows with -limit < log2 ((area / median area) / (apex / median apex)) < limit. Rows with a non-finite or non-positive area, apex or ratio are dropped.


CentrePSMs
3
Number of identifications per peptide ion, ranked by the summed intensity of their matched fragment ions, whose intensity weighted scan time centres the trace. It is applied after TopKPSMs, which ranks by ModelScore. At least 1.


RequirePeakAtScanTime
true
true quantifies only a peak that contains the weighted scan time of the identifications, so an ion without such a peak gets no row. The labeled partner needs a peak of its own trace that contains the fitted scan time of the ion. Without one it is not quantified, and the quality filter then drops the row with N15Labeling, and with N15LabelingOnly when the missing partner is heavy. false takes the peak with the closest apex when no peak contains the scan time.




The wavelet parameters:



Parameter
Default
Meaning




Borderpadding
None
Number of points padded at both ends of the trace. None derives it from the data.


BorderPadMethod
Padding.BorderPaddingMethod.Random
How the border points are filled (Random or Zero).


InternalPaddingMethod
Padding.InternalPaddingMethod.LinearInterpolation
How small gaps inside the trace are filled.


HugeGapPaddingMethod
Padding.HugeGapPaddingMethod.Zero
How gaps longer than HugeGapPaddingDistance are filled.


HugeGapPaddingDistance
100.
Gap length from which a gap counts as huge.


MinPeakDistance
Some 0.1
Peaks closer than this (in minutes) are merged. The distance is at least 1.5 times the median point spacing of the trace, which is also what None uses.


MinPeakLength
Some 0.1
Smallest peak width the wavelet scales start at.


MaxPeakLength
1.5
Largest peak width the wavelet scales go up to.


NoiseQuantile
0.01
Quantile of the wavelet correlation used as noise level.


MinSNR
0.01
A peak needs a correlation above MinSNR times the noise level.




The default file is QuantificationParams.json. To run without baseline correction set BaseLineCorrection = None in the script below.
Writing a parameter file
open ProteomIQon
open ProteomIQon.Domain
open FSharp.Stats.Signal

let waveletParams : WaveletParameters =
    {
        Borderpadding          = None
        BorderPadMethod        = Padding.BorderPaddingMethod.Random
        InternalPaddingMethod  = Padding.InternalPaddingMethod.LinearInterpolation
        HugeGapPaddingMethod   = Padding.HugeGapPaddingMethod.Zero
        HugeGapPaddingDistance = 100.
        MinPeakDistance        = Some 0.1
        MinPeakLength          = Some 0.1
        MaxPeakLength          = 1.5
        NoiseQuantile          = 0.01
        MinSNR                 = 0.01
    }

let quantificationParams : Dto.QuantificationParams =
    {
        PerformLabeledQuantification = Labeling.N15Labeling
        XicExtraction =
            {
                ScanTimeWindow = 2.
                MzWindow_Da    = Window.Estimate
                XicProcessing  = XicProcessing.Wavelet waveletParams
                TopKPSMs       = None
                IonMobilityWindow = Window.Fixed 0.05
            }
        BaseLineCorrection = Some { MaxIterations = 10; Lambda = 6; P = 0.05 }
        QualityFilterLog2Limit = 2.
        CentrePSMs = 3
        RequirePeakAtScanTime = true
    }

// Replace the temp folder with your project folder.
let outputPath = System.IO.Path.Combine(System.IO.Path.GetTempPath(), "QuantificationParams.json")

Json.serializeAndWrite outputPath quantificationParams

Outputs
The columns of the .quant file:



Column
Description




StringSequence
Amino Acid sequence (one-letter code) from PeptideDB which matches the psm candidate


GlobalMod
Indicator, if a peptide ion species is labeled or unlabeled


Charge
Precursor ion charge state


PepSequenceID
Unique identifier of the unmodified peptide sequence, which points to PeptideDB


ModSequenceID
Unique identifier of the modified peptide sequence (including PTMs, e.g., methylation), which points to PeptideDB


PrecursorMZ
Theoretical m/z of the ion plus the m/z correction, the m/z the XIC is centred on


MeasuredMass
Mass that corresponds to PrecursorMZ, in Dalton


TheoMass
Theoretical peptide mass in the spectrum (based on amino acid composition) in Dalton


AbsDeltaMass
Absolute difference between MeasuredMass and TheoMass


MeanPercolatorScore
Mean ModelScore of the identifications of the ion


QValue
Q-value (False-Discovery-Rate) based on combined model scores


PEPValue
Posterior Error Probability


ProteinNames
Protein Names out of the PeptideDB


QuantMz_Light
Mass-to-charge ratio from the extracted XIC of the unlabeled peptide ion


Quant_Light
Peak area from the extracted XIC of the unlabeled peptide ion


MeasuredApex_Light
Measured Apex of unlabeled peak


Seo_Light
Standard Error of Prediction for quantification


Params_Light
Describes the shape of the fitted peak for the unlabeled version of a peptide. Contains information about peak height, estimated peak time, and peak width.


Difference_SearchRT_FittedRT_Light
Difference between the retention time originally determined using PSMs and the retention time calculated from the measured peak


KLDiv_Observed_Theoretical_Light
Describes how well the measured unlabeled isotope pattern matches the theoretically expected pattern.


KLDiv_CorrectedObserved_Theoretical_Light
Corrected Kullback-Leiber divergence of isotopic pattern of unlabeled peptide ion versus the measured pattern


QuantMz_Heavy
Mass-to-charge ratio from the extracted XIC of the labeled peptide ion


Quant_Heavy
Peak area from the extracted XIC of the labeled peptide ion


MeasuredApex_Heavy
Measured Apex of labeled peak


Seo_Heavy
Standard Error of Prediction of quantification


Params_Heavy
Describes the shape of the fitted peak for the labeled version of a peptide. Contains information about peak height, estimated peak time, and peak width.


Difference_SearchRT_FittedRT_Heavy
Difference between the retention time originally determined using PSMs and the retention time calculated from the measured peak


KLDiv_Observed_Theoretical_Heavy
Describes how well the measured labeled isotope pattern matches the theoretically expected pattern.


KLDiv_CorrectedObserved_Theoretical_Heavy
Corrected Kullback-Leiber divergence of isotopic pattern of labeled peptide ion versus the measured pattern


Correlation_Light_Heavy
Correlation calculated based on Pearson between unlabeled and labeled peaks


QuantificationSource
If spectra are found over Alignments or Peptide Spectrum Matching


IsotopicPatternMz_Light
M/z-distribution of isotope cluster in spectra for unlabeled peaks


IsotopicPatternIntensity_Observed_Light
Observed intensity distribution of unlabeled isotopic clusters


IsotopicPatternIntensity_Corrected_Light
Corrected intensity distribution of unlabeled isotopic clusters


RtTrace_Light
Retention Time Profile of unlabeled peptide ion


IntensityTrace_Observed_Light
Intensity trace over for an observed unlabeled isotopic peak cluster


IntensityTrace_Corrected_Light
Corrected intensity trace between an unlabeled peak and a measured isotopic peak cluster


IsotopicPatternMz_Heavy
M/z-distribution of isotope cluster in spectra for labeled peaks


IsotopicPatternIntensity_Observed_Heavy
Observed intensity distribution of labeled isotopic clusters


IsotopicPatternIntensity_Corrected_Heavy
Corrected intensity distribution of labeled isotopic clusters


RtTrace_Heavy
Retention Time Profile of labeled peptide ion


IntensityTrace_Observed_Heavy
Intensity trace for an observed labeled isotopic peak cluster


IntensityTrace_Corrected_Heavy
Corrected intensity trace between a labeled peak and a measured isotopic peak cluster


AlignmentScore
NaN in PSM based rows. In transferred rows the probability from AlignmentBasedQuantStatistics that the quantified peak is the ion's peak


AlignmentQValue
0 in PSM based rows. In transferred rows the q-value from AlignmentBasedQuantStatistics


IonMobility
Ion mobility of the identifications, weighted by their matched fragment intensity, NaN without ion mobility


IonMobilityCentre
Ion mobility the XIC of the row is summed around, NaN without an ion mobility window




Running the tool
Install with dotnet tool install --global ProteomIQon.PSMBasedQuantification, then quantify one run:
proteomiqon-psmbasedquantification -i path/to/run.mzlite -ii path/to/run.qpsm -d path/to/database.db -o path/to/output -p path/to/QuantificationParams.json

Several runs, paired by position in the two lists, three in parallel:
proteomiqon-psmbasedquantification -i path/to/run1.mzlite path/to/run2.mzlite path/to/run3.mzlite -ii path/to/run1.qpsm path/to/run2.qpsm path/to/run3.qpsm -d path/to/database.db -o path/to/output -p path/to/QuantificationParams.json -c 3

Two directories, paired by file name:
proteomiqon-psmbasedquantification -i path/to/mzliteFolder -ii path/to/qpsmFolder -d path/to/database.db -o path/to/output -p path/to/QuantificationParams.json -c 3 -mf

All flags:
proteomiqon-psmbasedquantification --help

title: AlignmentBasedQuantification
content:
AlignmentBasedQuantification
QuantBasedAlignment predicts where a peptide ion identified in another run should elute in
this run. AlignmentBasedQuantification extracts the ion chromatogram (XIC) of every transferred ion around that prediction, decides which
of the peaks in the XIC belongs to the ion, and fits that peak as PSMBasedQuantification does.
The decision is made by a model that each run learns from the ions it identified itself. The output is a .quant file with the run's own
quantifications followed by the transferred ones, which
AlignmentBasedQuantStatistics then scores.

How a peak is chosen
For each transferred ion:


The XIC is extracted over ±ScanTimeWindow around PredictedScanTime, baseline corrected, and its peaks are detected with the
wavelet or second derivative method of the PSM based quantification.


Candidates are the peaks whose position lies within ±max(MinScanTimeWindow, ScanTimeWindowSdFactor · PredictedScanTimeSd) of the
prediction, at most ±ScanTimeWindow. With the defaults this is ±1 min where the alignment is precise and up to ±2 min where it is not.

Each candidate gets the features below.
A logistic regression gives each candidate a probability of being the ion's peak. The candidate with the highest probability is fitted.

A peak is always chosen when any candidate lies in the window, so this step never rejects an ion. Ions whose analyte is absent from the run are
handled by AlignmentBasedQuantStatistics, which uses the decoy transfers described below.



Feature
What it measures




scan time distance
|candidate − PredictedScanTime| in units of PredictedScanTimeSd (at least 0.03 min), and its square


shape correlation
correlation of the candidate with the source trace, shifted onto the candidate


relative height
log10 of the candidate height relative to the highest candidate


width ratio
|log2| of the ratio of the widths at half height of candidate and source trace


number of candidates
log2 of the number of candidates in the window


isotope evidence
correlation of the M0 and M+1 traces over the candidate, and log2 (M+1 / M0)


mass error
|ppm| of the M0 m/z around the candidate apex


ion mobility distance
|candidate ion mobility − PredictedIonMobility| in units of PredictedIonMobilitySd (timsTOF only)




The model is trained per run on the ions the run identified itself and that QuantBasedAlignment also transferred (overlap ions). For
these the right answer is known: the candidate within one standard deviation of the apex of the run's own PSM based peak. Only overlap ions with a
reliable own fit (|search − apex of the fitted peak| < 2 standard deviations of the fitted peak) are used. The training is cross-fitted: the peptides are split into 5 folds, and an
overlap ion is decided by the model trained on the other four folds. New ions are decided by the model trained on all overlap ions. A run with fewer than 200
training ions uses a fixed score instead: −0.5 · min(d², 50) + 4 · shape correlation + 2 · log10 relative height, with d the scan time
distance.

In the figure four peaks lie in the candidate window. The highest is 0.6 min from the prediction. The model chooses the
peak next to the prediction, whose shape matches the source trace. It is the peak of the run's own identification.
An ion that cannot be quantified gets no row, for example when no candidate lies in the window, the XIC is too short, or the peak
detection or the fit fails. The reason is in Status of .alignfeatures.
m/z window
The tool measures the offset between observed and theoretical m/z in the MS1 spectra of ions the run quantified itself. After removing
outliers it fits the offset in ppm as the sum of a function of scan time and a function of m/z. Every trace of an ion (monoisotopic,
isotopes, labeled partner) is centred on its theoretical m/z plus the correction at the PredictedScanTime and that m/z.
With MzWindow_Da set to Estimate the half width is 4 standard deviations of the offsets that remain after the correction, the same at
every m/z. Fixed sets the half width in Da and keeps the correction.
With fewer than 50 measured ions left, the correction is fitted on the precursor m/z of the .quant file instead, and Estimate uses a
half width of 0.05 Da.
Ion mobility
Ion mobility is used when the spectra and the .align file have it. An XIC point is then the sum of the intensity of all peaks inside
the m/z window and inside the ion mobility window, as in PSMBasedQuantificationTIMs. Both widths are part of the quantity, so transferred
and PSM based quantities are comparable when both tools use the same widths.
The traces of an ion, of its isotopes and of its labeled partner share one window, set by XicExtraction.IonMobilityWindow. The
expected ion mobility of the ion is PredictedIonMobility, or its ion mobility in the source run when the .align row has no prediction.


Fixed v: ±v around the ion mobility centre of the ion. The centre is the intensity weighted ion mobility of the signal within v of
the expected ion mobility, around the PredictedScanTime. Without such signal it is the expected ion mobility.

Estimate: ±max(0.05, 4 · PredictedIonMobilitySd) 1/K0 around the expected ion mobility, ±0.05 without prediction.

In a transferred row, IonMobility is the intensity
weighted ion mobility of the chosen peak, measured within one fitted standard deviation of its apex. IonMobilityCentre is the ion
mobility the traces were summed around: the centre with Fixed, the expected ion mobility with Estimate, NaN without ion mobility.
Labeled quantification
With PerformLabeledQuantification other than Unlabeled the partner of the other label is extracted with the same windows. Its peak
is the peak that contains the fitted scan time of the ion. With RequirePeakAtScanTime set to false, the peak with the closest apex is
taken when none contains it. A partner that cannot be quantified keeps its m/z and traces but gets no quantity, and the row is kept. The ion's own peak is
always the candidate chosen by the selection model.
An ion that the run did not quantify itself is not transferred when the PSM based row of its labeled partner has a fitted peak and a
quantity of the ion's label. Its Status is labeled partner quantified by its PSM based row.
Inputs and outputs



Flag
Meaning
Comes from




-i
.mzlite of the run, or a directory
MzMLToMzLite or MzMLToMzLiteIonMobility


-ii
.align of the run, or a directory
QuantBasedAlignment


-iv
.quant of the same run, or a directory
PSMBasedQuantification or PSMBasedQuantificationTIMs


-d
peptide database (SQLite)
PeptideDB


-o
output directory, created when missing



-p
parameter file (JSON)
this page


-mf
switch: pair the files by base name instead of by position



-dc
switch: write <run>_mzCorrection.html with the m/z offsets and their correction



-c
number of runs processed in parallel, one core each, default 1





Without -mf the files are paired by position, the files of a directory sorted by name. If the numbers of files differ, the tool stops.
<run>.quant has the layout of the PSM based .quant files. It holds the PSM based rows with a fitted peak, then one row per quantified
transferred ion with QuantificationSource = Alignment. These rows pass no quality filter. In these rows Difference_SearchRT_FittedRT is PredictedScanTime minus the fitted
scan time. AlignmentScore and AlignmentQValue hold NaN until AlignmentBasedQuantStatistics fills them.
<run>.alignfeatures is a tab separated table with one row per .align row. AlignmentBasedQuantStatistics reads it from the directory of
the aligned .quant and uses its features. The main columns:



Column
Meaning

the ion


CandidateProbability
probability of the chosen candidate, nan with the fixed score


CandidateMargin
lead of the chosen candidate over the second best


NCandidates

SelectionModel

position of the chosen candidate, in minutes

Status
quantified, or why the ion was not quantified




With DecoyFraction above 0, <run>.aligndecoy holds the decoy transfers: a share of the new ions quantified a second time with
PredictedScanTime shifted by 4 to 6 minutes, where their own peak is not. A decoy is skipped when the ion's own peak could lie in its XIC. Each row has the .quant columns, the shifted PredictedScanTime and
the .alignfeatures columns. AlignmentBasedQuantStatistics uses them to estimate how often an ion whose analyte is absent from the run
passes the q-value cutoff. They never enter <run>.quant.
Logs go to AlignmentBasedQuantification_log.txt and one <run>_log.txt per run, with the counts of ions per reason at Info level and
each ion that was not quantified at Debug level.
Parameters



Parameter
Default
Meaning

Also quantify the partner of the other label. Unlabeled quantifies only the ion itself, for label-free data. N15Labeling, N15LabelingOnly and Labelshift behave the same here.

How the XIC is extracted and processed.

Some { MaxIterations = 10; Lambda = 6; P = 0.05 }
Asymmetric least squares baseline of the XIC. None switches it off.

Default

open ProteomIQon.Domain
open FSharp.Stats.Signal

    {
        Borderpadding          = None
        BorderPadMethod        = Padding.BorderPaddingMethod.Zero

        NoiseQuantile          = 0.01

    }

let alignmentBasedQuantificationParams : Dto.AlignmentBasedQuantificationParams =
    {
        // Labeling.Unlabeled for label-free data
        PerformLabeledQuantification = Labeling.N15Labeling
        XicExtraction =
            {
                ScanTimeWindow = 2.
                MzWindow_Da    = Window.Estimate
                XicProcessing  = XicProcessing.Wavelet waveletParams
                TopKPSMs       = None
                IonMobilityWindow = Window.Estimate
            }
        BaseLineCorrection     = Some { MaxIterations = 10; Lambda = 6; P = 0.05 }
        MinScanTimeWindow      = 1.
        ScanTimeWindowSdFactor = 8.
        DecoyFraction          = 0.2
        Seed                   = 1
        RequirePeakAtScanTime  = true
    }

// Replace the temp folder with your project folder.
let outputPath =
    System.IO.Path.Combine(System.IO.Path.GetTempPath(), "AlignmentBasedQuantificationParams.json")

Json.serializeAndWrite outputPath alignmentBasedQuantificationParams

Running the tool
Install the tool with dotnet tool install --global ProteomIQon.AlignmentBasedQuantification.
Quantify one run:
proteomiqon-alignmentbasedquantification -i path/to/run.mzlite -ii path/to/run.align -iv path/to/run.quant -d path/to/peptides.db -o path/to/output -p path/to/AlignmentBasedQuantificationParams.json

Process every run in a set of directories, paired by file name, four at a time:
proteomiqon-alignmentbasedquantification -i path/to/mzlite -ii path/to/align -iv path/to/quant -d path/to/peptides.db -o path/to/output -p path/to/AlignmentBasedQuantificationParams.json -mf -c 4

Print the description of every argument:
proteomiqon-alignmentbasedquantification --help

Limitations

MinScanTimeWindow (1 min) and ScanTimeWindow (2 min) are fixed in minutes and do not scale with the gradient length.
The fixed score uses the same weights in every run.
The right peak must be among the detected peaks. Shoulders that the peak detection merges with a neighbour cannot be chosen separately.

title: LabeledProteinQuantification
content:
LabeledProteinQuantification
In a 15N metabolic labeling experiment one sample grows on 15N, is mixed with the 14N sample, and both versions of every peptide are measured in the same run, so the ratio of the light and the heavy peak is a direct comparison of the two samples. How the label enters the search is described in BioFSharp.Mz, and how the ratio is formed from the two peaks in the quantification chapter. LabeledProteinQuantification takes the .quantAndProt rows from JoinQuantPepIonsWithProteins and aggregates them to one light intensity, one heavy intensity and one ratio per protein group and run. It works in up to four steps. The first step is mandatory: every row already holds a light and a heavy intensity, the step divides them into Ratio_LightByHeavy and merges the rows identified from the light and from the heavy form of the same peptide ion. The second step merges charge states and the third merges modified forms of a peptide, both optional. The fourth merges all peptides of a protein group. Every step transforms, filters and aggregates light, heavy and ratio separately.

Inputs and outputs



Flag
Meaning
Comes from




-i
one or more .quantAndProt files, or a directory that is searched for *.quantAndProt
JoinQuantPepIonsWithProteins


-o
the output directory, created when missing



-p
the parameter file in JSON
this page




Logs go to LabeledProteinQuantification_log.txt and LabeledQuantification_log.txt in the output directory.
The tool writes up to five tab separated tables into the output directory. GlobModAggregation.txt is the result of the first step, one row per peptide ion and run with Quant_Light, Quant_Heavy and Ratio_LightByHeavy. ChargeAggregation.txt appears only when the charge step runs and ModificationAggregation.txt only when the modification step runs. ProteinAggregation.txt has one row per protein group and run with the aggregated light, heavy and ratio values, and for each the number of values used, CV, standard deviation and SEM. LabeledQuant.txt is the same table pivoted, one row per protein group and one block of columns per input file, named <run>.Ratio_LightByHeavy, <run>.Quant_Heavy and so on. RatioLFQ reads this file to turn the ratios into comparable intensities per run.
Parameters



Parameter
Default
Meaning




Correlation_Light_Heavy_Threshold
None
Some 0.9 keeps only rows whose light and heavy elution profiles correlate above 0.9. None keeps everything. The filter is applied in the first step.


Alignment_QValue
Some 0.05
Rows that came from alignment and have an alignment q-value at or above this value are dropped. PSM based quantifications carry the q-value 0, and rows without an alignment q-value are kept. None keeps every row.


ModificationFilter
UseModifiedPeptides.All
Which peptides enter the aggregation. All keeps every peptide, No drops every peptide with a modification, UseOnly mods keeps unmodified peptides and peptides whose modifications are all in the list.


AggregateGlobalModificationsParams
{ LabeledTransform = None; LabeledSingleFilters = None; LabeledGroupFilters = None; LabeledAggregation = { Light = Mean; Heavy = Mean; Ratio = Mean } }
The first step, always run.


AggregatePeptideChargeStatesParams
None
Some params runs the charge step with the given AggregationParams. None skips it.


AggregateModifiedPeptidesParams
None
Some params runs the modification step. None skips it.


AggregateToProteinGroupsParams
{ LabeledTransform = None; LabeledSingleFilters = None; LabeledGroupFilters = None; LabeledAggregation = { Light = Mean; Heavy = Mean; Ratio = Mean } }
The protein step, always run.




An AggregationParams record describes one step. Each of its fields has a Light, a Heavy and a Ratio entry, so the three value series can be treated differently.



Parameter
Default
Meaning




LabeledTransform
None
Some { Light = Some Log2; Heavy = Some Log2; Ratio = Some Log2 } applies a NumericTransform (Log2, Add, Substract, MultiplyBy, DivideBy) before filtering and aggregation. None inside means no transform for that series.


LabeledSingleFilters
None
Some { Light = None; Heavy = None; Ratio = Some (seq [IsSmallerThan 0.0]) } keeps only values that pass every NumericFilter (IsBiggerThan, IsSmallerThan) of their series.


LabeledGroupFilters
None
Some { Light = Some (seq [Tukey 1.5]); Heavy = None; Ratio = None } removes outliers within each group before aggregation. GroupFilter is Tukey factor, Stdev factor or TopX count.


LabeledAggregation
{ Light = Mean; Heavy = Mean; Ratio = Mean }
How the remaining values of a group are combined per series. NumericAggregation is Mean, Median or Sum.




Five default files exist, all with Alignment_QValue set to Some 0.05. LabeledQuantificationParams.json is the table above. LabeledQuantificationParams_withCorrFilter.json sets Correlation_Light_Heavy_Threshold to Some 0.9. LabeledQuantificationParams_CorrFilter_ChargeAgg.json sets the threshold to Some 0.0 and adds the charge step with Mean. LabeledQuantificationParams_CorrFilter_ChargeAgg_ModAgg.json sets the threshold to Some 0.0 and adds the charge and the modification step, both with Mean. LabeledQuantificationParams_Transform_Filter_Sum.json log2 transforms light, heavy and ratio in the first step, keeps only log2 ratios below 0.0 there, and sums light and heavy in the protein step while the ratio is still averaged.
Writing a parameter file
open System.IO
open ProteomIQon

// Used for the first step and the protein step of the default file: no transform, no filters, mean of light, heavy and ratio.
let meanOfAll : Common.LabeledProteinQuantification.AggregationParams =
    {
        LabeledTransform     = None
        LabeledSingleFilters = None
        LabeledGroupFilters  = None
        LabeledAggregation   =
            {
                Light = NumericAggregation.Mean
                Heavy = NumericAggregation.Mean
                Ratio = NumericAggregation.Mean
            }
    }

let labeledQuantificationParams : Dto.LabeledQuantificationParams =
    {
        Correlation_Light_Heavy_Threshold  = None
        Alignment_QValue                   = Some 0.05
        ModificationFilter                 = UseModifiedPeptides.All
        AggregateGlobalModificationsParams = meanOfAll
        AggregatePeptideChargeStatesParams = None
        AggregateModifiedPeptidesParams    = None
        AggregateToProteinGroupsParams     = meanOfAll
    }

// Replace the temp folder with your project folder.
let outputPath = Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), "LabeledQuantificationParams.json")

Json.serializeAndWrite outputPath labeledQuantificationParams

Running the tool
The tool installs with dotnet tool install --global ProteomIQon.LabeledProteinQuantification. A single run:
proteomiqon-labeledproteinquantification -i path/to/run.quantAndProt -o path/to/output -p path/to/LabeledQuantificationParams.json

Several runs in one table, from a list or from a directory:
proteomiqon-labeledproteinquantification -i path/to/run1.quantAndProt path/to/run2.quantAndProt -o path/to/output -p path/to/LabeledQuantificationParams.json
proteomiqon-labeledproteinquantification -i path/to/quantAndProt -o path/to/output -p path/to/LabeledQuantificationParams.json

All flags:
proteomiqon-labeledproteinquantification --help

title: AlignmentBasedQuantStatistics
content:
AlignmentBasedQuantStatistics
A peptide ion transferred by QuantBasedAlignment and quantified by
AlignmentBasedQuantification has no identification in the run, so nothing yet says
whether the quantified peak is the ion. AlignmentBasedQuantStatistics gives every such ion two values:

AlignmentScore: the probability that the quantified peak is the ion's peak, given that the analyte is present in the run.

AlignmentQValue: the estimated share of false quantifications among the new ions of the run that score at least as well. A quantification is
false when the chosen peak is not the ion's peak or, unless AbsentAnalyteFdr is Off, when the analyte is absent from the run.


New ions are the transferred ions without a PSM based quantification in the run.
JoinQuantPepIonsWithProteins reads the output.
LabelFreeProteinQuantification and
LabeledProteinQuantification filter on the q-value only if their Alignment_QValue parameter
is set. They then drop transferred rows with a q-value at or above it. All their default files set it to Some 0.05, and None keeps every transferred row.

Training data and label
The tool learns from overlap ions: ions that a run identified and quantified itself and that were also transferred to it. For them the run's
own PSM based peak is the reference. Let z be the distance between the transferred peak and the own peak, in units of the own peak's standard
deviation.



Label
Condition
Use




right
z ≤ PositiveRtSdFactor (1) and |log2 (transferred / own quantity)| ≤ MaxAbsLog2QuantRatio (1)
training


ambiguous
PositiveRtSdFactor < z ≤ NegativeRtSdFactor (3), same quantity bound
left out of training


wrong
everything else
training




Overlap ions whose own peak cannot serve as reference (no fitted peak, or a width or quantity that is not positive) get no label.
Features
All features come from the transferred row of AlignmentBasedQuantification and the .align row. None uses the ion's own PSM row, so the
features of an overlap ion look like those of a new ion.



Group
Features




scan time
residual to PredictedScanTime (signed, absolute, per peak sd, per local alignment error), the local alignment error, peak width and its ratio to the source peak


mass and isotopes
|ppm| of the monoisotopic peak, intensity weighted |ppm| over the isotope peaks, number of isotope peaks, similarity of the isotope pattern to the source, KL divergences to the theoretical pattern


chromatogram
correlation with the source trace (around the peak and over the whole XIC), DTW distance to the source trace, competing peaks in the XIC, share of the XIC maximum at the apex, XIC length, relative SEO


ion
source quantity and apex intensity, source scan time, m/z, charge


selection
from <run>.alignfeatures: Sel_NCandidates, Sel_IsoCorr, Sel_IsoRatioLog2, Sel_ShapeCorr, Sel_RtZ, Sel_ImZ, Sel_LogRelHeight, Sel_AbsLog2FwhmRatio, and Sel_CandidateProbability, Sel_CandidateMargin when all runs used the same selection model


ion mobility
|IonMobility − PredictedIonMobility| / PredictedIonMobilitySd (timsTOF only)




The local alignment error of an ion is the median |own PSM scan time − PredictedScanTime| of the run's overlap ions predicted within ±2 min.
Every run needs <run>.alignfeatures next to its aligned .quant.
UseIntensityRatioFeatures adds four features: the ratios of target to source quantity and apex intensity, and the target quantity and apex
intensity. They are off by default: a model that prefers a ratio near 1 penalises peptides that really changed between the samples.
Model, calibration and q-values

The overlap ions of all learning runs are pooled and split into 5 folds by peptide sequence, so the forms of a peptide stay together.

Per fold, a gradient boosted tree model (ML.NET FastTree) is trained on the right and wrong ions of the other four folds. Unless
AbsentAnalyteFdr is Off, the decoys of the learning runs join this training as wrong examples, in the fold of their peptide.


Per fold, an isotonic calibration (the share of right ions as a non-decreasing function of the raw score) is fitted on the right and
wrong overlap ions of the held-out fold. It turns scores into probabilities. Below the lowest fitted score the probability follows a logistic
fit of the label on the raw score. A fold with fewer than 200 such ions, or with one label only, is calibrated on the held-out ions of all folds.
If those are too few or of one label as well, the logistic fit alone is used.

The AlignmentScore p of a new ion is the mean of the calibrated probabilities of the 5 fold models.

The posterior error probability of a new ion is 1 − p. Per run, the new ions are sorted by p in descending order. The AlignmentQValue of
an ion is the mean posterior error probability of all new ions with at least its p, made monotone.


Unless AbsentAnalyteFdr is Off, the absent-analyte rate at the ion's score (see Absent analytes) is added to the q-value, which is made
monotone again.


The highest probability the isotonic calibration can give grows with the number of right and wrong overlap ions it is fitted on: about
0.99 up to 2,000 ions, 0.999 from 20,000. With few overlap ions a cutoff of q ≤ 0.01 can therefore keep few or no transferred ions.
The log reports an out-of-fold check. Each overlap ion is scored by the fold model that did not see it and calibrated on the held-out
ions of the other folds (by the logistic fit alone if those are too few or of one label). The true share of wrong peaks is given at
q ≤ 0.01, 0.05 and 0.1, once with the ambiguous ions counted as wrong and once without them.
Absent analytes
The overlap ions are present in the run, so they cannot show how the model scores an ion whose analyte is absent. The decoy transfers
of AlignmentBasedQuantification (<run>.aligndecoy) are used for that. Per run, the absent-analyte rate at score t is
FDR_absent(t) = π · (decoys with p ≥ t / all decoys) · N_new / N_new(p ≥ t)
with N_new the number of new ions of the run and π the fraction of new ions whose analyte is absent. Estimated estimates π per run as
Storey does, with λ = 0.5. Conservative sets π to 1.

A run with fewer than 200 decoys uses the decoys of all runs to score.
Decoys without a fitted peak and new ions without an alignment row count as p = 0.

When a run to score or to learn from has no <run>.aligndecoy next to its aligned .quant (AlignmentBasedQuantification writes none
with DecoyFraction 0), or no decoy has a fitted peak, the tool warns and works as Off.


Inputs and outputs



Flag
Meaning
Comes from




-i
PSM based .quant of the runs to score
PSMBasedQuantification or PSMBasedQuantificationTIMs


-ii
.align of the runs to score
QuantBasedAlignment


-iii
aligned .quant of the runs to score
AlignmentBasedQuantification


-l
PSM based .quant of the runs to learn from
as -i


-ll
.align of the runs to learn from
as -ii


-lll
aligned .quant of the runs to learn from
as -iii


-o
output directory, created when missing



-p
parameter file (JSON)
this page


-mf
switch: pair the files by name instead of by position



-c
number of runs read and written in parallel, one core each, default 1



-ts
switch: write the training ions of each learning run



-dc
switch: write AlignmentScoreHistogram.html





Each flag takes one file, several files, or a directory. The runs to learn from are usually the runs to score. Without -mf the files are
paired by position, the files of a directory sorted by name, and the numbers of files must agree.
For every scored run the tool writes <run>.quant with the layout of the input .quant files: the PSM based rows of -i and one row per new
ion with AlignmentScore and AlignmentQValue. When the PSM row of an overlap ion has no fitted peak, the transferred row replaces it and is
scored like a new ion. -ts writes <run>.quanttestset per learning run, with the overlap ions, their label, fold, raw and calibrated
out-of-fold score, out-of-fold q-value and features. Logs go to AlignmentBasedQuantStatistics_log.txt, with the features, the out-of-fold
check and the calibration per score bin and per source intensity quartile, and to one <run>_log.txt per run.
Parameters



Parameter
Default
Meaning




PositiveRtSdFactor
1.0
A peak within this many own peak sd is right.


NegativeRtSdFactor
3.0
Up to this many sd a peak is ambiguous, beyond it wrong.


MaxAbsLog2QuantRatio
1.0
Right and ambiguous peaks need |log2 (transferred / own quantity)| at most this.


UseIntensityRatioFeatures
false
Add target to source intensity ratios as features.


UseIonMobility
true
Add the ion mobility feature when the rows have a finite IonMobility and the .align file a PredictedIonMobilitySd above 0.


NumberOfFolds
5
Cross-validation folds.


Trainer
FastTree
FastTree or LightGbm. LightGbm needs the native library lib_lightgbm, which the package ships for win-x64, linux-x64 and osx-x64.


NumberOfLeaves, NumberOfTrees, MinimumExampleCountPerLeaf, LearningRate
null
null takes the trainer's defaults: 20, 100, 10, 0.2 for FastTree; 31, 100, 20, 0.1 for LightGbm.


AbsentAnalyteFdr
Estimated
Off, Estimated or Conservative: whether and how the absent-analyte rate enters the q-value (see Absent analytes).

1
Seed of the folds and of the trainer.




See the default parameter file.
Writing a parameter file

    {
        PositiveRtSdFactor         = 1.
        NegativeRtSdFactor         = 3.
        MaxAbsLog2QuantRatio       = 1.
        UseIntensityRatioFeatures  = false
        UseIonMobility             = true
        NumberOfFolds              = 5
        Trainer                    = "FastTree"
        // empty: the defaults of the trainer
        NumberOfLeaves             = System.Nullable()
        NumberOfTrees              = System.Nullable()
        MinimumExampleCountPerLeaf = System.Nullable()
        LearningRate               = System.Nullable()
        AbsentAnalyteFdr           = "Estimated"
        Seed                       = 1
    }

// Replace the temp folder with your project folder.
let outputPath =
    System.IO.Path.Combine(System.IO.Path.GetTempPath(), "AlignmentBasedQuantStatisticsParams.json")

Json.serializeAndWrite outputPath alignmentBasedQuantStatisticsParams

Running the tool
Install the tool with dotnet tool install --global ProteomIQon.AlignmentBasedQuantStatistics.
Score every run, learn from all of them, pair the files by name, and work on four runs at a time:
proteomiqon-alignmentbasedquantstatistics -i path/to/quant -ii path/to/align -iii path/to/aligned -l path/to/quant -ll path/to/align -lll path/to/aligned -o path/to/output -p path/to/AlignmentBasedQuantStatisticsParams.json -mf -c 4

Add -ts to keep the training ions and -dc for the score histogram. Print the description of every argument:
proteomiqon-alignmentbasedquantstatistics --help

Limitations


The false discovery rate of absent analytes is an estimate from decoys at a shifted scan time. Analytes near the detection limit are not
modelled.

The model needs overlap ions. With few identifications per run, or runs that share few ions, there is little to learn from.

title: QuantBasedAlignment
content:
QuantBasedAlignment
In data dependent acquisition a peptide ion quantified in one run is often present in another run without having been fragmented there.
QuantBasedAlignment predicts where such an ion elutes in the run that lacks it. For every target run (-i) it learns, from the peptide
ions the target shares with each source run (-ii), how scan times shift between the two runs. With that model it predicts the scan time
of every source ion in the target, together with an error estimate for each prediction. For timsTOF runs it also predicts the ion mobility.
The tool is the first of three that transfer quantifications between runs. It reads the .quant files of
PSMBasedQuantification or PSMBasedQuantificationTIMs.
AlignmentBasedQuantification then looks for the peak of each transferred ion, and
AlignmentBasedQuantStatistics scores the result.

How the scan time model works
The tool works on each pair of target and source run separately.


The model uses the ions (sequence, modifications, charge) that both runs quantified with a successful peak fit whose identification
scan time lies within two standard deviations of the apex of the fitted peak. A pair needs at least 20 shared ions.


It describes the shift target scan time − source scan time as a function of the source scan time. Each point of the curve is the
median shift of the k shared ions nearest in source scan time. Between ions the curve is interpolated linearly, beyond the first and last
ion it is constant.


Some shared ions have a wrong peak in one of the two runs and lie far from the true shift. Before the final fit, up to three rounds
remove ions whose residual exceeds max(3 · 1.4826 · MAD, 0.05 min), where MAD is the median absolute deviation of the
residuals.

k is chosen from 5, 7, 11, 15, 21, 31, 41, 51, 71 and 101 by 5-fold cross-validation on the median absolute error, with folds by peptide sequence. -s seeds the folds.

The sources of a target are ranked by their median absolute out-of-fold error. Each ion is transferred from the best ranked
source that has it.


PredictedScanTimeSd is 1.4826 times the median absolute out-of-fold error of the shared ions within ±5 min of the ion's
source scan time, and at least 0.01 min. With fewer than 10 ions in the window the scale of the whole pair is used. It is small where the runs
agree and large where they do not, for example at the end of the gradient.


Only source ions that pass the filter of step 1 are transferred.
Ions the target quantified itself, called overlap ions, are transferred too, because the two following tools learn from them. They get the prediction of the fold
that did not contain them, so their errors are comparable to those of new ions.

The figure shows the scan time shift of a pair of runs. Grey points are shared ions, orange points are the shared ions that the tool trimmed.
The blue line is the running median and the band is ± PredictedScanTimeSd.
Ion mobility
The tool aligns the IonMobilityCentre of the .quant rows. When both runs of a pair have finite values on the shared ions, it fits the same model to the ion mobility shift over the source
ion mobility. Its trimming floor is 0.005 1/K0, its error scale uses the shared ions within ±0.05 1/K0 and is at least 0.001.
The results go into PredictedIonMobility and PredictedIonMobilitySd. Without ion mobility both columns hold nan. There is no switch.
Inputs and outputs



Flag
Meaning
Comes from




-i
one or more .quant files of the target runs, or a directory that is searched for *.quant
PSMBasedQuantification or PSMBasedQuantificationTIMs


-ii
one or more .quant files of the source runs, or a directory that is searched for *.quant
same


-o
the output directory, created when missing



-s
seed of the cross-validation folds, default 1



-dc
switch: write <run>_ScanTimeModels.html with the shifts, curves and out-of-fold errors per source



-c
number of targets aligned in parallel, one core each, default 1





There is no parameter file. A target is never its own source, so the same directory can be passed to -i and -ii.
The tool stops when an input path does not exist, when the paths of -i or those of -ii hold no .quant file at all, and when two input files from different directories have the same name.
For every target the tool writes <run>.align, tab separated, one row per transferred ion. The first 16 columns hold the ion, its m/z, PredictedScanTime, and the scan time, intensities, traces and IonMobility of the ion in its source run, where IonMobility is the ion mobility centre of the ion in that run.
Five columns follow.



Column
Meaning




PredictedScanTimeSd
local error scale of PredictedScanTime, in minutes


SourceFileName
source run of the ion, without extension


SourceModelError
median absolute out-of-fold error of the model of this source, in minutes


PredictedIonMobility
predicted ion mobility in the target, nan without ion mobility


PredictedIonMobilitySd
local error scale of PredictedIonMobility, nan without ion mobility




<run>.alignmetric holds the out-of-fold predictions of one fold. No later tool reads it. Logs go to QuantBasedAlignment_log.txt and one <run>_log.txt per target. Per pair they give the numbers of shared and removed
ions, the chosen k and the out-of-fold errors. A target without any source that shares 20 ions with it gets a warning.
Running the tool
Install the tool with dotnet tool install --global ProteomIQon.QuantBasedAlignment.
Align every run of an experiment against all others, four at a time:
proteomiqon-quantbasedalignment -i path/to/quant -ii path/to/quant -o path/to/align -c 4

Align one target against two sources:
proteomiqon-quantbasedalignment -i path/to/target.quant -ii path/to/source1.quant path/to/source2.quant -o path/to/align

Print the description of every argument:
proteomiqon-quantbasedalignment --help

Limitations

The trimming floor (0.05 min) and the error scale window (±5 min) are fixed.
Pairs with fewer than 20 shared ions are skipped. Runs with few identifications get few or no sources.
Every target is fitted against every source, so the run time grows with the square of the number of runs.
The tool is meant for runs of one organism on one LC setup. Fractionated samples and DIA data are not supported.
